def write_noanalysis_reads(in_file, region_file, out_file, config):
    """Write a BAM file of reads in the specified region file that are not analyzed.

    We want to get only reads not in analysis regions but also make use of
    the BAM index to perform well on large files. The tricky part is avoiding
    command line limits. There is a nice discussion on SeqAnswers:
    http://seqanswers.com/forums/showthread.php?t=29538
    sambamba supports intersection via an input BED file so avoids command line
    length issues.
    """
    amba is a nice tool for this, but it is not available on all systems.
        """
        # Write the reads to a temporary file.
        temp_file = out_file + ".tmp"
        with pysam.Samfile(in_file, "rb") as in_sam:
            with pysam.Samfile(temp_file, "wb", template=in_sam) as out_sam:
                for region in region_file.fetch():
                    # Get the read names for the reads in this region.
                    region_reads = set(in_sam.references[region.tid].split())
                    # Get the read names for the reads in this region.
                    for read in in_sam.fetch(region.tid, region.start, region.end):
                        if read.qname not in region_reads:
                            out_sam.write(read)
        # Copy the header from the input file.
        with pysam.Samfile(in_file, "rb") as in_sam:
            with pysam.Samfile(out_file, "wb", header=in_sam.header) as out_sam:
                # Copy the reads.
                with pysam.Samfile(temp_file, "rb") as temp_sam:
                    for read in temp_sam:
                        out_sam.write(read)
        # Remove the temporary file.
        os.remove(temp_file)
